about: The 26 franchises of Krish's Dog Viral Creative System playbook (Google Sheet 1v3VgCjD8Zrh0WrxLNFisTQ1sGbgdUJfqRR97SmgYGa4, 9 Nov 2026), graded for how Heartside can make them: A = stills or a carousel carry the joke; B = one short motion beat or Heartside's inner-voice film; R = realism stretch, motion a viewer cannot tell from footage (Krish, 10 Nov: "Photorealistic AI dogs doing things a viewer cant quite tell is real or not - anything is on the cards"); nothing is excluded since Krish's 10 Nov ruling ("I want A plan with zero shackles, none whatsoever"). The evidence links and creators stay in the Sheet, not in this public repository. Read with docs/plans/2026-11-10-sprint-120.md.

grades.R: realism stretch: photoreal motion a viewer cannot tell from footage, held to floor real-dogs and real-behavior-in-motion

franchises.name: The Human-Arms Lip-Sync
franchises.why: Krish's pick, 10 Nov ("This is Good"): a dog in a hoodie with a hidden person's arms, every lyric of a song everyone knows staged literally, one beat a second, lyrics on screen. Reference read: YouTube Short u7s47cIeh6M, 32 s, 18.8M views at read (Apify run tf6hbOlGdAEgbm0Mh). Generated as photoreal shots per lyric line, cut to the track.
franchises.timeline: 0.0-1.5s premise line on the opening scene ("My dog's ..."), the only on-screen text; then two shots per sung line, 1.5 to 2 s each, each staged literally by the dog with human arms, with a reaction from the dog in every shot; end on a physical gag held 2 s. No lyric captions (Krish, 10 Nov: "I don't think we ever need subtitles for videos for song lyrics."). The song is added in the platform.
franchises.comment_prompt: Which line is your dog? Quote it.

concepts.payoff: the dog checks out, and the gift is the real mug

franchises.name: The Trend Dance Reskin
franchises.why: Krish's pick, 10 Nov ("We should Generate a realistic version of this with dog's"): YouTube Short WzzueiNf-uU, 20 s, about 247,000 views when read (Apify run KHIGZqR4EiHadqBfe). Its sound is Bronski Beat, "Smalltown Boy" (Shazam match at 29.6 s into the song, Apify run EFcaZGnLgV5O26HVN), the viral 80s dance trend: 72K Shorts on the sound, top ones at 10M, 7.2M and 7M views (Krish's screenshot, 10 Nov). Two small animals stand upright and do the trend's moves into a low ultra-wide lens, close-up each, then the synced two-shot. Riding a trending sound with its known dance is the distribution.
franchises.timeline: 0-6s pup A close-up doing the trend moves into the low ultra-wide lens; 6-12s pup B close-up, paws on head; 12-18s both side by side in sync; 18-24s the ending gag (one dog flops and keeps dancing on its back). No on-screen text: the trend sound and the picture carry the premise (playbook: "use text only to clarify the premise"); the caption names the trend. Sound: Smalltown Boy, added in the app from the trend's start point.
franchises.comment_prompt: Tag the person whose dog would actually do this.

reskin_rule: Krish, 2026-11-10: "stop being a priest when it comes to putting good backing tracks and copying memes and video content. It is acceptable." Proven memes, formats, edits and tracks are reskinned and reused directly; a winner's frames may be used as generation references. Heartside's twist is the dog, the line and, on signature posts, the real product at the end.
